strengths: Novel theoretical framework interpreting classifier-free guidance as tempered posterior sampling with principled decomposition of geometry-aware prior and observation likelihood terms
Well-engineered multiscale graph architecture balancing local geometric fidelity with efficient global message propagation on large complex unstructured meshes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple complementary metrics, sensor strategies, observation densities, and thorough ablations demonstrating consistent improvements
Strong empirical results particularly in sparse observation regime (25-57% RRMSE reduction vs supervised baselines, 23-33% SSIM improvement), addressing practically relevant setting
Realistic test domain with complex building geometry and high Reynolds number (Re ≈ 2×10^7) from actual urban neighborhood rather than synthetic cases
Clear presentation with well-structured narrative, detailed technical appendices, and effective visualizations of methodology and results
weaknesses: Work limited to 2D horizontal slices despite motivation requiring volumetric 3D understanding for urban air quality monitoring; misleadingly claims extensibility to 3D without demonstrating it

Generalization claims substantially overstated: all 'unseen geometries' are different altitudes of same Bristol neighborhood; lacks evaluation on genuinely different cities/urban domains, making scope narrow

Critical practical concerns unaddressed: (1) robustness to measurement noise never empirically tested despite η in observation model (Eq. 1), (2) no computational cost analysis despite real-time monitoring motivation, (3) observation operator assumes perfect node alignment whereas real sensors interpolate

Weak comparison with classical data assimilation: only compares against Low-Cost SVD rather than widely-used Ensemble Kalman Filter or modern variational methods (3D-Var, 4D-Var); overstates advantages of avoiding linearization/adjoints

Inconsistent sensor generalization: trajectory-based observations (mobile sensors, key application) show 19% RRMSE degradation vs training distribution; only single qualitative example provided despite importance

CFG guidance weight γ fixed at 2.0 with no principled selection method for new domains; empirical optimization on single dataset limits transferability; classical DA analogy to error covariance weighting not formalized rigorously
Uncertainty quantification claimed in abstract but never evaluated: no ensemble spread vs error analysis or calibration assessment, undermining stochastic DA motivation
Steady-state analysis only despite mentioning streaming sensors and real-time prediction; temporal dynamics critical for environmental monitoring but deferred to future work
Mesh decimation strategy for multiscale graph designed for single domain; unclear if fixed offline decimation generalizes to truly unseen urban geometries

Missing ablation studies: limited evidence that multiscale architecture doesn't harm performance (claimed in text but MS-MGN baseline results don't strongly support), no analysis of what model learns for physics constraints

strengths: Solid technical quality with rigorous mathematical formulation (posterior decomposition, score additivity, tempered posterior interpretation)
Strong empirical results demonstrating 25-57% RRMSE reduction and 23-33% SSIM improvement over supervised baselines and classical DA methods
Thoughtfully designed multiscale graph architecture balancing local geometric fidelity with efficient global communication
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including multiple observation densities, sensor sampling strategies, and proper statistical reporting with error bars
Valuable practical contribution: generalization across unseen geometries, wind directions, and observation densities without retraining
Insightful interpretation of classifier-free guidance as tempered posterior sampling connects generative modeling to classical DA concepts
Honest presentation with clearly acknowledged limitations regarding 2D steady-state focus and future work needs
Extensive implementation details in appendices supporting reproducibility (hyperparameters, architecture, training procedures)
weaknesses: Severely limited to 2D horizontal slices extracted from 3D data; claims of 'direct extensibility to volumetric domains' lack demonstration, fundamentally compromising applicability since urban wind flows are inherently 3D
Steady RANS assumption ignores temporal dynamics essential for real environmental monitoring; dynamic flows are deferred to future work
Narrow experimental scope: single urban domain (Bristol), single Reynolds regime, no real sensor data validation—generalization to other cities/conditions undemonstrated

Technical novelty is incremental: primarily combines established techniques (diffusion models, CFG from Ho & Salimans 2021, Multiscale MeshGraphNets); application to this problem is novel but not methodology
Ensemble uncertainty quantification claimed but never validated: no analysis of whether ensemble spread correlates with error or properly represents posterior uncertainty
Physics constraints not enforced: model doesn't ensure incompressibility (∇·u = 0), which should hold for RANS fields but is untested
Robustness to measurement noise completely untested; all experiments use noiseless perfect observations, unrealistic for real sensors

Reproduction concerns: no code availability mentioned, dataset URL incomplete, γ = 2.0 selected 'empirically' without principled justification, computational cost (training time, inference latency) entirely omitted
Sensor dropout training (p_uc = 0.1 drops all sensors) for unconditional branch lacks rigorous justification; unclear if this produces true geometry-aware prior vs. default flow behavior

strengths: Well-motivated interpretation of classifier-free guidance as tempered posterior sampling, providing elegant connection between guided diffusion and classical data assimilation theory
Thoughtfully designed multiscale graph architecture (o2o/o2r/r2r/r2o) effectively balancing local flow-geometry interactions with global information propagation across complex urban meshes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple observation densities (0.1%-2.6% coverage), sensor sampling strategies, held-out sensor interpolation, and ablation studies
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, promised code availability, dataset clearly described, baselines well-specified, transparent limitations discussion
Demonstrates meaningful generalization to held-out mesh geometries and wind directions within the studied urban-flow distribution without retraining
Strong empirical results with 25-57% RRMSE improvement and 23-33% SSIM improvement over deterministic and classical DA baselines
Produces uncertainty-aware ensembles with demonstrated calibration (CRPS analysis, Wasserstein distance), not just point estimates
Addresses practical real-world problem of urban wind field reconstruction from sparse sensor networks
weaknesses: Severe scope limitation: all experiments restricted to 2D steady-state horizontal slices from a single urban neighborhood (Bristol); generalization to other cities/building layouts/terrain remains completely unexplored, undermining claims of scalability and geometry-awareness

Limited baseline comparisons: missing direct comparison with closely related Diff-SPORT method; relies partly on dated classical methods (POD-3DVar 2006); no recent physics-informed neural networks or modern surrogate-based DA approaches included
No validation on real sensor data: all observations are noiseless perfect CFD samples; robustness to sensor noise, bias, calibration drift, and missing data—critical for deployment—is not analyzed

Computational cost not reported: inference requires T=20 diffusion steps on multiscale GNN, but no timing comparisons with baselines (e.g., LCSVD/POD-3DVar likely orders of magnitude faster); GPU requirements and inference latency for real-time applications not discussed

Hyperparameter sensitivity: guidance weight γ shows severe instability at higher densities (Table 5: RRMSE=0.481 at γ=3.0 with 8000 observations); no principled method for selecting γ on new domains; empirical tuning on tested domain only

Generalization claims overstated: test on 'held-out altitude slices' is not true geometry generalization (all slices horizontal cuts of same neighborhood); tested sensor configuration generalization shows moderate degradation and only covers random-to-clustered distribution shifts

Physics consistency not enforced: method does not constrain to PDE residuals, mass conservation, or boundary conditions; RANS training data errors not analyzed or propagated; physically unplausible reconstructions not discussed

Missing practical considerations: no analysis of robustness to observation noise, wind direction estimation error, or sensor calibration issues; comparison of computational cost and inference latency critical for real-time environmental monitoring not provided

Methodological novelty moderate: CFG is established technique (Ho & Salimans 2021); multiscale message-passing standard (MeshGraphNets); contribution primarily problem formulation and integration rather than new methods
Analysis of failure modes limited: errors concentrated in shear layers/wake boundaries identified but not deeply analyzed; performance across diverse flow regimes and extreme sparsity not explored
